Undergraduate Programmes

Details of the undergraduate programme in Mechanical Engineering are to be found in Chapter 9. All courses extend over one term only, and consist of 3 hours of lectures per week unless otherwise specified. In general, the only prerequisites are the core courses, unless otherwise specified.
Course Descriptions

courses.label: ME 100
courses.title: Introductory Survey of Law
paras: The rights and responsibilities of the engineer as a citizen of Ontario and Canada under the law; brief history of Canadian law differentiating between Civil and Criminal Law, the rights and duties of citizens and police, a review of Domestic Law, Reali Estate Law, Landlord and Tenant Law. The law as it may pertain to the engineer in his profession, brief reviews of the Laws of Contracts, Patents, Trade marks, industrial design, and copyright, Bills of Exchange, Company Law, incorporation of companies. Common and Preferred shares, the Law of Master and Servant, Surveying Law, Constitutional Law, Private International Law, and other topics. This course is restricted to senior Mechanical Engineering students.

courses.label: ME 116
courses.title: Engineering Concepts 2
paras: A continuation of Gen E 115 with applications of graphics, measurement and other analytic principles to introductory problems in the various disciplines of Mechanical engineering; an introduction to engineering design methods as applied to Mechanicat Engineering and including specification development, information-gathering, concept ‘ formulation, feasibility analysis and report writing. Prereq: Gen E 115

courses.label: ME 200
courses.title: Introduction to Mechanical Engineering 1 Discussion of Structure of Mechanical Engineering curriculum, operation of Department, Faculty,
paras: University, technical societies.

M E 201 FLW Advanced Calculus infinite series: Tests for absolute; conditional, uniform convergence; power series; series expansions; differentiation and integration. Partial differentiation: total derivatives; estimation of errors; chain rule; geometry; maxima and minima; Taylor series; Jacobians. Multiple integration: areas, centroids, moments of inertia, centres of gravity. Vector analysis: gradient divergence, curl, Laplacian; integral theorems.

courses.label: ME 202
courses.title: Statistics for Engineers (Equivalent to M Sci 21)
paras: Frequency distributions; measures of central tendency; standard deviation and other measures of dispersion; moments, skewness, kurtosis. Probability, Binomial, Poisson, normal, multinomial distributions. Theory of sampling and statistical estimation. Tests of hypotheses; significance. The t-test and chi-squared test. Curve fitting by least squares. Correlation and regression. Analysis of variance. Experimental design.

courses.label: ME 203
courses.title: Ordinary Differential Equations
paras: First and simple higher order equations. Solution of linear equations. Solution of linear equations by various methods; equations transformable to linear form. Simuitaneous equations. Laplace transforms. Series solutions. Fourier series.
Course Descriptions Mechanical Engineering

courses.label: ME 204
courses.title: Numerical Analysis
paras: A survey of numerical procedures witn emphasis upon computer implementation using the WATFIV programming language. !n particular, the following topics are covered: Interpolation, curve fitting, solution of non-linear equations, numerical integration, numerical solution of ordinary differential equations, matrix algebra and solution of systems of linear equations, and problems in the soiution of partial differential equations.

courses.label: ME 212
courses.title: Dynamics
paras: An introduction to the kinematics of particle and rigid body motion. Ilmpulse-momentum equations. Work-energy methods and Euler’s equations. Simple gyroscopes. Vibrations.

courses.label: ME 215
courses.title: Structure and Properties of Materials
paras: The relevance of materiais to engineering practice. The microstructure of materials, crystallinity and crystal imperfections, glasses and amorphous solids. Elastic and plastic deformation in metals, viscoelasticity of plastics, fracture of brittle and ductile solids. Electrical and magnetic properties of materials.

courses.label: ME 219
courses.title: Mechanics of Deformable Solids 1
paras: An analytical treatment of statics and resistance of materials. Equilibrium of particles, rigid bodies and deformable bodies. Vector fields. Introduction to Stress and Strain. Stress-strain relationships. Elastic and inelastic behaviour of prismatic members subjected to axial, shearing, torsional and flexural deformations.

courses.label: ME 220
courses.title: Mechanics of Deformable Solids 2
paras: A generat treatment of the behaviour of structural components from the study of stress and strain in solids. Topics include super-position, energy theorems, theories of failure, elastic and inelastic analysis of symmetrical bending, torsion of circular members, columns and stability, and virtual work.

courses.label: ME 230
courses.title: Control of Properties of Materials
paras: Phase equilibria, non-equilibrium behaviour, heat treatment of metais, diffusion, strengthening processes. Alloying, composite materials, cold and hot working. Failure of engineering materials: creep, fatigue, corrosion and other environmental degradation processes. Prevention of service failures.

courses.label: ME 250
courses.title: Thermodynamics
paras: The engineering science of energy. The scope and limitations of thermodynamics. Macroscopic approach to heat, work, energy and the First Law. Properties and state of simple substances. Controlmass and control-volume energy analysis. The Second Law of Thermodynamics, principle of increase of entropy, limiting cycle efficiencies, criteria for equilibrium.

courses.label: ME 300
courses.title: Introduction to Mechanical Engineering 2 Technical specialties in Mechanical Engineering, discussion of options in Mechanical Engineering
paras: curriculum, seminars and technical topics in the various options.

courses.label: ME 305
courses.title: Partial Differential Equations
paras: Modelling physical systems with distributed parameters. Boundary and initial conditions. Division into hyperbolic, parabolic and elliptic equations by means of discriminant.

Characteristics. Separation of variables; eigenvalues and eigenfunctions. Orthogonality. Fourier series. Gamma functions. Bessel and Legendre equations. Numerical solution of Laplace and diffusion equations. Analogue simulation techniques.

courses.label: ME 321
courses.title: Kinematics and Dynamics of Machines
paras: Principles of the geometry of motion. Uniform and non-uniform motion, linkage, gears, cams. Synthesis and analysis of mechanisms. Consideration of the dynamic forces in machines. Gyroscopic torque. Vibration analysis, response to shock, motion and force transmissibility, vibration isolation.

courses.label: ME 322
courses.title: Mechanical Design 1
paras: Analysis and synthesis of machine elements. Factors affecting working stresses, fatigue, creep and impact considerations. Design of shafting, springs, screws, clutches, brakes and gears.

courses.label: ME 340
courses.title: Manufacturing Processes
paras: The principles of ‘manufacturing unit processes including casting, forming, machining and joining. Interactions between design, materials (metals, polymers, ceramics) and processes. Advantages and limitations, relative cost, and production rates of competitive processes.
Course Descriptions ; 405 Mechanical Engineering

courses.label: ME 351
courses.title: Fluid Mechanics 1
paras: Physical properties of fluids and fundamental concepts in fluid mechanics. Hydrostatics. Conservation laws for mass, momentum and energy. Flow similarity and dimensional analysis as applied to engineering problems in fluid mechanics. Laminar and turbulent flow. Engineering applications such as flow measurement, flow in pipes and fluid forces on moving bodies. Introduction to compressible flow.

courses.label: ME 353
courses.title: Heat Transfer 1
paras: Introduction to heat transfer mechanisms. The formulation and solution of steady and transient heat conduction. Radiant heat transfer inciuding exchange laws and view factors. introductory convective heat transfer.

courses.label: ME 354
courses.title: Thermodynamics 2
paras: Emphasis on applications of thermodynamics to flow processes, real fluids, evaluation of state functions of real fluids. Non-reacting mixtures, reacting mixtures, equilibrium considerations. Introduction to the kinetic theory of gases.

courses.label: ME 360
courses.title: Introduction to Control Systems
paras: Open loop and feedback control. Laws governing mechanical electrical, fluid and thermal control components. Analogies. Analysis of some engineering contro! systems using block diagram algebra, transient and steady-state operations. Different modes of control. Review of Laptace Transform methods. Concepts of stability. Principles of analogue computer simulation. Brief treatment of linear flow graphs and bondgraphs.

courses.label: ME 362
courses.title: Fluid Mechanics 2
paras: Basic equations of two-dimensional flow, exact viscous solutions, introduction to lubrication, boundary layers, and introduction to turbulence. Turbomachinery fundamentals and applications. Selected advanced topics.

courses.label: ME 400
courses.title: Introduction to Mechanical Engineering 3 Research frontiers in Mechanical Engineering,
paras: specific discussion of research done at Waterloo, seminars by members of research group.

courses.label: ME 423
courses.title: Mechanical Design 2
paras: This is a continuation of the M E 322 course in analysis and synthesis of machinery, including advanced analysis of machine elements such as clutches, brakes, couplings, journal bearings and gears. The latter part of the course includes advanced machine design concepts such as reliability, optimization and techniques for stimulating innovative design. A synthesis project involving the machine elements studied is usually included.
Prereq: M E 322

courses.label: ME 432
courses.title: Physical Metallurgy of Deformation and Fracture
paras: Microscopic origins of elastic and an elastic behaviour. Plastic flow at low and high temperatures with emphasis on the microscopic mechanisms and their application to engineering design. Deformation mechanism maps. Types of fracture and micromechanism fracture maps. Application of fracture mechanics. Fatigue and cyclic hardening behaviour. Environmental effects.

courses.label: ME 435
courses.title: Industrial Metallurgy
paras: This course is intended for those students interested in acquiring a working knowledge of metallurgy. It will cover: Metals and alloy systems, iron-carbon alloys, heat treatment and the function of alloying elements in steel, corrosion and scale resistant alloys, copper and nickel base alloys, light metals and their alloys; casting, hot and cold working of metals; soldering, brazing and welding; corrosion and oxidation; metal failure analysis.

courses.label: ME 443
courses.title: Metal Casting Processes
paras: Moulding from the liquid state. Review of applicable heat transfer and fluid theory. Influence of time in casting. Solidification time, freezing waves and riser design. Pouring time, fluidity, grating and running. Hot tears, distortion, shrinkage and residual stresses. Die casting; thermal stability, pressure pulse effects. Other casting methods.

courses.label: ME 448
courses.title: Production Engineering: Design of Manufacturing Systems
paras: The interaction and relationship of manufacture to the factory organization. Product design and devetopment, planning and control of production. Principles of mass and flow production. Machine loading and line balancing. Design analysis and evaluation techniques of plant layout and materials handling systems as basic components of a manufacturing facility and system.
Course Descriptions Mechanical Engineering

courses.label: ME 452
courses.title: Energy Transfer in Buildings
paras: Thermodynamic properties of moist air; psychometric charts; humidity measurements; direct water contact processes; heating and cooling of moist air by extended surface coils; solar radiation; heating and cooling of loads on buildings; effects of the thermal environment; air conditioning and calculations; air flow In and around buildings, diffusers.

courses.label: ME 456
courses.title: Heat Transfer 2
paras: Selected topics in heat transfer fundamentals and applications. Topics to be covered include the fundamentats of convection with analytical solutions to simple Jaminar fiow problems and approximate solutions to turbulent flow problems based on analogies between momentum and heat transfer. Also covered is radiant exchange in grey enclosures and in black enclosures containing emittingabsorbing gases. The remaining topics will be chosen from design of heat exchangers; condensation heat transfer; boiling heat transfer, and the treatment of problems in heat conduction.

courses.label: ME 459
courses.title: Energy Conversion
paras: Review of reserves and consumption trends of Canada’s and the world’s energy resources. Design of fossil-fuel central power plants including boiler efficiency calculations and advanced steam and binary cycles. Review of atomic physics including fission and fusion energy. Design of nuclear fission power plants including design of reactor core for critical conditions, fuel cycles and radiation hazards. Design considerations for solar energy conversion devices including: availability of solar energy, solarthermal converters, thermal storage and photovoltaics. Principles of fuel cells and some aspects of their design. Other topics as appropriate.

courses.label: ME 462
courses.title: Introduction to Automation
paras: Number systems, Codes and Coding, minimization techniques applied to design of logic systems. Comparison of microprocessors, memories, input/output logic elements; design and application of Digital systems for data collection, and control of pneumatic, hydraulic and mechanical systems; comparison of software and hardware techniques in such applications.

courses.label: ME 463
courses.title: Tribology 1
paras: The science of friction, lubrication and wear. The topography and contact mechanics of real surfaces. The measurement of friction and wear. Friction and wear theories for elastic and plastic contact. Lubrication mechanisms; hydrostatic, hydrodynamic, elastohydrodynamic, boundary, extreme pressure, and solid film. Physical and chemical properties of lubricants. Bearings and their selection.

courses.label: ME 469
courses.title: Introduction to the Environmental Sciences
paras: Compésition and structure of the atmosphere and oceans. Thermodynamics of moist air. Hydrostatic equation. Stability. Winds and current on a rotating earth gradient, geostropic and inertial flow. Vertical variation of wind, convection, thermals, plumes, basic diffusion theory-coastal currents, gulf streams, tides, internal waves.

courses.label: ME 482
courses.title: Mechanical Engineering Projects
paras: Engineering assigments requiring the student to demonstrate initiative and assume responsibility. Student activity is guided and co-ordinated by a faculty supervisor. In selecting projects, particular account is taken of the student's field of specialization. Projects, in general, involve technical disciplines beyond the strictly mechanical engineering field.

courses.label: ME 524
courses.title: Advanced Dynamics and Stress Analysis in Design
paras: This course is related to M E 423, although M E 423 is not an essential prerequisite. M E 524 brings together dynamics and stress analysis in an application to design of dynamic machinery. Basic kinematic and dynamic concepts are reviewed and extended, Lagrangian and computer simulation methods are introduced. Basic stress analysis methods are reviewed and indeterminate structures are discussed, along with finite-element and other computer techniques. A design project (involving synthesis), utilizing the concepts studied, is usually included.

courses.label: ME 525
courses.title: Mechanica! Vibrations in Machines
paras: Fundamentals of mechanical vibration. Forced, transient and nonlinear vibrations. Numerical methods for multi-degree-of-freedom systems. Continuous systems. Vibration isolation. Measurement of vibration. Use of models and the analogue computer.
Course Descriptions 407 Mechanical Engineering

courses.label: ME 527
courses.title: Mechanics of Deformable Solids 3
paras: Analysis of stress and strain in three dimensions, plates and shells, stress functions, plastic stressstrain concentrations. Residual stress, thermal stress and creep. Energy methods.
Physical Metallurgy of Structures and Transformations .

Nucleation and growth in metals. Diffusion and sintering. Fundamental aspects of condensed phase equilibrium in binary and.ternary metal systems. Non-equilibria in metal systems. Surface phenomena. Corrosion and oxidation in metals. Applications to industrial metals and alloys.

courses.label: ME 534
courses.title: Non-metailic Materials
paras: Structure of amorphous and crystalline plastics. Polymerization, control of properties of plastics by crosslinking and additives. Glasses, properties of fibers, refractories, abrasive materials, oxides, carbides, properties and applications of graphite. Brittle fracture, viscoelasticity and rheological models.

courses.label: ME 541
courses.title: Deformation Processes
paras: Principles of deformation processes including forging, rolling, drawing, extrusion and sheet metalworking. Basic methods of analysing pressures, forces and deformation. Process control
‘and limitations. Interaction of process, equipment
and material; workability.

courses.label: ME 544
courses.title: Welding
paras: Features and advantages of the various welding processes, Welding arc characteristics. Temperature distributions around welds. Metallurgy of the weld metal and heat affected zone in various alloys, — including carbon and stainless steels, and aluminum alloys. Origin of various weld defects and methods of detecting them. Static and dynamic design of welded joints. Residual stresses, distortion and fracture of welds.

courses.label: ME 548
courses.title: Numerical Control of Machine Tools 1
paras: Data storage and processing. Basic requirements of a Numerically Controlled System. Analysis of Numerically Controlled Machine Tools and their effect on the performance of the servo-drive system. Data preparation. Programming for Numerically Controlled Machine Tools. Advantages and economies of Numerically Controlled Machine Tools. Prereq: M E 462 or permission of instructor.

courses.label: ME 557
courses.title: Combustion 1
paras: Combustion thermodynamics; Introduction to chemical kinetics of combustion; Combustion properties of fuels; Flammability of combustible mixtures. Flame propagation mechanisms, pre-mixed and diffusional; Stability of flames; Introduction to combustion aerodynamics, jet flames; Atomization; Droplet and spray combustion; Elementary ignition concepts and theory; Basic detonation theory.

courses.label: ME 561
courses.title: Fluid Power Control Systems
paras: Properties of hydraulic fluids. Design and function of conventional hydraulic and pneumatic circuits. Characteristics of flow and pressure control valves. Speed control in fluid power circuits. Performance of pumps and fiuid motors. Hydrostatic and hydrokinetic transmission systems. Principles of sealing, filtration and heat contro! in hydraulic circuits. Industrial applications of fluid power systems.

courses.label: ME 563
courses.title: Turbomachines
paras: Classification of turbomachines, performance parameters and laws of modelling. Basic equation of flow in turbomachines, compressible flow. Energy transfer in radial and axial turbomachines, performance characteristics, losses and efficiencies. Blade and cascade design, three-dimensional effects.

courses.label: ME 565
courses.title: Gas Dynamics
paras: Basic laws of compressible fiuid flow. Wave propagation in compressible fluids, isentropic flow of a perfect gas, normal and oblique shock waves. Prandt!-Meyer flow. Flow in ducts and over bodies, flow with friction (Fanno) and heat transfer (Rayleigh), imperfect gas effects, measurement of compressible flows, use of formulae, charts and tables, introduction to the methods of characteristics.

courses.label: ME 566
courses.title: Fluid Mechanics 3
paras: Reynolds stresses, intensity and scale of turbulence. The “law of the wall’, logarithmic velocity profile and velocity defect laws, effects of roughness. Pressure loss in pipes and conduits. Jets and wakes. Flow in diffusers and contractions, and experimental measurement techniques.
Course Descriptions Mechanical Engineering

courses.label: ME 568
courses.title: Noise Analysis and Control
paras: Basic acoustics. Legal aspects. Physiology of the ear. Signal analysis. instruments and techniques. Noise reduction techniques, absorption, damping and barrier. Wave transmission and impedance. Handling industrial plant noise problems. Designing for minimum noise in engineering systems.

courses.label: ME 569
courses.title: Fluid Mechanics-Design Topics
paras: A study of the design aspects of fluid mechanics, Unsteady flow, pipe and duct systems, two and three dimensional flow techniques, practical calculation of boundary layers, separation, base pressures, jets, wakes and shear layers, diffusers and flow distribution devices, flow control, two-phase flow, instrumentation, wind tunnel modelling, wind loading. The course will be oriented to practical design techniques for flow systems, reactors, air pollution control equipment, etc.
Air Pollution 1

Nature and sources of air pollution, chemical and biological aspects, effects on health and environment. Physical aspects of the atmosphere, thermodynamics, vertical variation of wind and temperature, stability, convection, atmospheric turbulence, diffusion equations, plumes, thermals, jets in stratified flow, radioactive plumes, particulate dispersion, instrumentation (micrometeorological), air pollution control techniques and equipment monitoring instrumentation.

Course Descriptions

courses.label: MUSIC 100G
courses.title: The Basics of Music
paras: An introduction to music terminology, techniques and styles, through lectures and listening, with examples from all eras of music history.

courses.label: MUSIC 101G
courses.title: Music Ensemble
paras: The study of selected music literature through rehearsals and performance in one of the Music Department’s ensembles: Choir, Concert Band, Orchestra. Regular attendance at rehearsals and performances is required. Offered on a pass/fail basis.

courses.label: MUSIC 102G
courses.title: Music Ensemble
paras: (See Music 101G for course description)

courses.label: MUSIC 125G
courses.title: Popular Music and Culture
paras: An examination of the popular music world and the interplay between rock, folk, jazz and gospel idioms and classical music. The social, commercia! and technological elements of popular music are considered.

courses.label: MUSIC 150G
courses.title: Introduction to Music |
paras: An introduction to music from early Christian chant to Beethoven through listening, lectures, discussion and analysis.
Course Descriptions 409 Music

courses.label: MUSIC 151G
courses.title: Introduction to Music 2
paras: An introduction to the music of the 19th and 20th centuries through listening, lectures, discussion and analysis. Compositions include symphonies, concertos, chamber music, operas, electronic, and computer music.
Prereq: Music 150G or consent of instructor.

courses.label: MUSIC 201G
courses.title: Music Ensemble
paras: (See Music 101G for course description)

courses.label: MUSIC 202G
courses.title: Music Ensemble
paras: (See Music 101G for course description)

courses.label: MUSIC 250G
courses.title: Music Theory 1 (Medieval and Renaissance)
paras: The study of scales, melody, two-part counterpoint, and basic harmonic concepts emphasizing the Middle Ages and Renaissance. Ear-training and sight-singing lab sessions will cover diatonic melodic and simple two-part exercises.
Prereq: A basic knowledge of scales, triads, and musical notation.

courses.label: MUSIC 251G
courses.title: Music Theory 2 (Baroque and Classical)
paras: The study of four-part homophonic and contrapuntal music, of diatonic and simple chromatic harmonies, and of elementary forms, emphasizing Baroque and Classical music. Ear-training and sight-singing lab sessions will cover four-part diatonic exercises. Prereq: Music 250G or permission of the instructor.

courses.label: MUSIC 253G
courses.title: Medieval and Renaissance Music
paras: The study of music that flourished under courtly and church patronage from the early Christian Church to 1600. Gregorian chant, liturgical drama, mass, motet, secular songs, and instrumental music are studied. Prereq: Music 150G and Music 151G or Music 100G or consent of the instructor.

courses.label: MUSIC 254G
courses.title: Baroque and Classical Music »
paras: The study of music of the Baroque and Classical eras from 1600 to 1800. A survey of major genres by Monteverdi, Schiitz, Purcell, Bach, Handel, Haydn, Mozart and others..
Prereq: Music 150G and Music 151G or Music 100G or consent of the instructor.

courses.label: MUSIC 262G
courses.title: Instrumental Literature 1
paras: A study of the music written for a variety of instrumental groups, such as chamber music, symphony, concerto. The course includes a laboratory component.
Prereq: Music 150G/151G or Music 100G or permission of instructor.

courses.label: MUSIC 266G
courses.title: Music Studio Private music studio in Voice, Piano, Organ,
paras: Classical Guitar and orchestral instruments. This
course is available only to Music majors and minors.
Prereq: Audition with Music Faculty. Studio Fee.

courses.label: MUSIC 267G
courses.title: Music Studio
paras: (See Music 266G for course description.)
Prereq: Music 266G and consent of Music Faculty. Studio Fee.

courses.label: MUSIC 273G
courses.title: Traditional Folk Music
paras: A delineation of the characteristic motifs in folk music as found in Great Britain, Canada, the United States and Australia. Various folk instruments will be introduced.

courses.label: MUSIC 274G
courses.title: Introduction to Jazz
paras: A survey of the development of jazz schools and individual styles as well as a study of melodic, harmonic, and rhythmic improvization. Styles will be demonstrated through recordings and live performance.

courses.label: MUSIC 275G
courses.title: Computer Applications in Music
paras: A survey of computer applications in music history, analysis and composition. Concepts from computer science and specific techniques and implementations of these various music activities are examined. Theoretical study is coupled with practical hands-on experience.
Prereq: Music 100G or 150G/151G or consent of instructor.
Course Descriptions Music

courses.label: MUSIC 280G
courses.title: Canadian Music
paras: An historical study of the development of music in Canada from colonial times to the present, with particular emphasis on the composers and music of the 20th century.
Prereq: Music 150G/151G or Music 100G or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Music Ensemble
paras: (See Music 101G for course description)

courses.label: MUSIC 302G

paras: (See Music 101G for course description)

courses.label: MUSIC 355G
courses.title: Music and Culture in Vienna
paras: A Spring seminar to be taught in Vienna and environs. The course includes daily lectures and attendance of music performances during the Vienna Music Festival, as well as tours of places relating to the culture of Vienna.
Prereq: Music 150G/151G or Music 100G or consent of instructor.

courses.label: MUSIC 366G
courses.title: Music Studio
paras: (See Music 266G for course description.)

courses.label: MUSIC 367G
courses.title: Music Studio
paras: (See Music 266G for course description.)

courses.label: MUSIC 370G
courses.title: Music Theory 3 (19th Century)
paras: The study of the harmonic, melodic, and formal aspects of 19th century music. Ear-training and sight-singing lab sessions will cover chromatic chord progressions and modulatory melodies.
Prereq: Music 250G/251G or consent of instructor.

courses.label: MUSIC 371G
courses.title: Music Theory 4 (20th Century)
paras: The study of the compositional aspects of 20th century music, including extended tonality, atonality, 12-tone writing, neo-classical idioms, and contemporary compositional procedures. Lab sessions will cover non-tonal melodic reading and complex chord structures.
Prereq: Music 370G.

courses.label: MUSIC 380G
courses.title: Directed Study in Music
paras: Prereq: Advanced standing in music and consent of instructor.

courses.label: MUSIC 467G
courses.title: Music Studio
paras: A continuation of Music Studio. A recital is required. Prereq: Music 466G and consent of Music Faculty. Studio Fee.

courses.label: MUSIC 490G
courses.title: Senior Honours Seminar
paras: A research seminar required of all honours students. The topics will vary from year to year depending on the interests of the students and instructor(s).

Course Descriptions
Students in other disciplines may register for Optometry courses onty upon the approval of the Director of the School of Optometry.

courses.label: OPTOM 100
courses.title: History and Orientation
paras: A brief history of the profession and the development of visual science; a consideration of legal and organizational development of optometry; the role of professional associations. The role and scope of optometry and its relationship to other professions and the community.

courses.label: OPTOM 104
courses.title: Anatomy of the Eye and Associated Structures
paras: The gross, microscopic and ultra structure of ocular tissues. The embryology and comparative anatomy of the eye will be emphasized. The relationship of the eye to the vascular supply of the head and the nervous system will be studied. This course is credited only upon completion of Optom 114. Coreq: Biol 201

courses.label: OPTOM 105
courses.title: General Pathology
paras: Basic disease processes, including inflammation, degeneration, neoplasia; pathogenic microbiology and related diseases; immunity and hypersensitivity; disease caused by physical agents; diseases of the organ systems.
Prereq: Biol 201, Optom 104

courses.label: OPTOM 106
courses.title: Geometrical Optics
paras: Reflection and refraction. Image formation. Optical
properties of plane and curved surfaces, prisms and .
thin lenses. Thick lens theory and jens systems. Ray construction. Optical and ophthalmic instruments. Polarization.
Prereq: Phys 121, 121L, 122, 122L, Math 113

courses.label: OPTOM 111
courses.title: Physiological Optics
paras: The eye as an optical instrument. Ametropia and emmetropia. The refracting mechanism. The stimulus to accommodation. Ocular transmission. Visual acuity and visual performance; stray light in the eye; analysis of the retinal stimulus pattern. Prereq: Optom 106

courses.label: OPTOM 114
courses.title: Anatomy of the Eye and Associated Structures
paras: A continuation of Optom 104.
Prereq: Optom 104

courses.label: OPTOM 115
courses.title: General Pathology
paras: A continuation of 105.
Prereq: Optom 105

courses.label: OPTOM 116
courses.title: Optometrical Optics
paras: Properties of ophthalmic glass and lenses, cylindrical lenses, prisms, prismatic effects, lens combinations. Laboratory work involves processing prescriptions and experiments in optics.

courses.label: OPTOM 241
courses.title: Physiological Optics
paras: Ocular motility: Kinematics of eye movements, muscle actions, measurements of eye movements, types of eye movements, innervational!l systems subserving eye movements, clinical application. Prereq: Optom 177

courses.label: OPTOM 242
courses.title: Clinical Optometry
paras: Lectures and laboratories on clinical techniques for examination of the optical properties of the eye. Prereq: Optom 111

courses.label: OPTOM 244
courses.title: Neurophysiology of Vision °
paras: The neural processing of colour, brightness, movement and form by the retina, lateral geniculate, cortex, superior colliculus and other brain centres. Neural Mechanisms underlying binocular depth perception, the accommodative response and eye movement.
Prereq: Optom 104/114
Course Descriptions 413 Optometry

courses.label: OPTOM 245
courses.title: Ocular Pathology
paras: Signs, symptoms, clinical detection of primary and secondary ocular disease; instrument techiques; record keeping, patient counselling, referral procedures; management of ocular emergencies; primary health care responsibilities.
Prereq: Optom 105/115

courses.label: OPTOM 246
courses.title: Optometrical Optics
paras: A continuation of 116, dealing with problems peculiar to bifocal and multifocal lenses. Aberratior of thin lenses and the design of lenses of ophthaimic use.
Prereq: Optom 116

courses.label: OPTOM 251
courses.title: Physiological Optics
paras: Binocular vision and perception: The binocular system; binocular integration and interaction; effec of disparate stimulation; perceived size, shape, direction, distance, motion, colour, illusions.

courses.label: OPTOM 252
courses.title: Clinical Optometry
paras: Lectures and laboratories on clinical techniques for examination of the optical properties of the eye. Prereq: Optom 241/242

courses.label: OPTOM 254
courses.title: Physiology of the Visual Systems
paras: The physiology of the smooth muscles of the eye, the extraocular striate muscles, the lacrimal apparatus, the cornea, the iris, the lens, the ciliary body and the vitreous body. Production and drainage of aqueous and related influences on intraocular pressure. The vascular supply of the eye.
Prereq: Optom 104

courses.label: OPTOM 255
courses.title: Ocular Pathology
paras: A continuation of 245.
Prereq: Optom 245

courses.label: OPTOM 259
courses.title: Light and Illumination
paras: Principles of radiometry and photometry; illumination and related factors involved in the design and control of the visual environment in relationship to the human visual system; lighting surveys.

courses.label: OPTOM 261
courses.title: Physiological Optics
paras: The perception of light. Spectral sensitivity of the eye. Photochemistry of the retina. Luminance discrimination. The Stiles-Crawford effect. Visual Acuity. Intermittent stimulation. Introduction to colorimetry.

courses.label: OPTOM 274
courses.title: Genetics for Optometrists
paras: (See Optom 514 for a detailed description) Coreq: Optom 245, 255

courses.label: OPTOM 401
courses.title: Physiological Optics
paras: A continuation of 261. Increment thresholds and Stiles mechanisms. The laws of colour mixture. Chromaticity diagrams. Colour matching and colour discrimination. Characteristics of normals and colour defectives. The design of visual colorimeters, anomaloscopes and of colour vision screening tests. Congenital and acquired defects of colour vision.

courses.label: OPTOM 402
courses.title: Clinical Optometry
paras: Case analysis of the nonstrabismic patient: case history, testing the health and integrity of the visual system, refractive tests, binocular relations, analysis, diagnosis, prognosis and modes of therapy.
Prereq: Optom 242, 252

courses.label: OPTOM 404
courses.title: Neurophysiology of Vision
paras: The neural processing of colour, brightness, movement and form by the retina, lateral geniculate, cortex, superior colliculus and other brain centres. Neural mechanisms underlying binocular depth perception, accommodative response and eye movement.

courses.label: OPTOM 405
courses.title: Ocular Pathology
paras: (See Optom 245 for detailed description)

courses.label: OPTOM 406
courses.title: Optometrical Optics
paras: The lecture course deals with problems involved in selecting, preparing and fitting ophthalmic materials. Optical, cosmetic and comfort requirements, and patient counselling are considered. The laboratory course provides experience in preparing and fitting materials to patients.
Prereq: Optom 116, 246
Course Descriptions Optometry

courses.label: OPTOM 407
courses.title: Optometric Specialties: Contact Lenses
paras: A series of lectures and laboratories on the principles and procedures of prescribing and fitting contact lenses.
Prereq: Optom 401, 402

Optom 408 Y Optometric Clinic The student is assigned to the various areas of the clinic and under the direct supervision of optometrists of the clinic staff, carries out routine Clinical investigations of patients.

courses.label: OPTOM 411
courses.title: Physiological Optics
paras: (See Optom 251 for detailed description)

courses.label: OPTOM 412
courses.title: Clinical Optometry
paras: Detection and evaluation of sensory and motor characteristics of vision in strabismus. Classifications, diagnosis, prognosis, modes of therapy for strabismus and amblyopia.
Prereq: Optom 302, 312, 402

courses.label: OPTOM 414
courses.title: Physiology of the Visual Systems
paras: The physiology of the smooth muscles of the eye, the extraocular striate muscles, lacrimal apparatus, cornea, iris, lens, ciliary body and vitreous body. Production and drainage of aqueous and related influences on intraocular pressure. The vascular supply of the eye.

courses.label: OPTOM 415
courses.title: Ocular Pathology
paras: A continuation of 405.
Préreq: Optom 405

courses.label: OPTOM 427
courses.title: Optometric Specialties: Aniseikonia and Low Vision Aids
paras: A series of lectures and jaboratories in examining low vision and aniseikonic patients with specific techniques described. Treatment and therapy will be included.
Prereq: Optom 401, 402

courses.label: OPTOM 428
courses.title: Spring Clinic
paras: Each student is required to complete 120 hours of clinical practice during the spring.
Prereq: Successful completion of Year 4 programme.

courses.label: OPTOM 500
courses.title: Optometrical Praxis
paras: Practice management; financial management, establishing a practice, interprofessional relations, office design, optometric assistants, professional associations..

courses.label: OPTOM 501
courses.title: Optometry Research Project
paras: Students with an interest in research may arrange with a professor to undertake a research project of mutual interest. This course serves as an alternative to Psych 357. Contact the course co-ordinator for details.

courses.label: OPTOM 502
courses.title: Advanced Contact Lens Practice
paras: A series of lectures and practical demonstrations of the principles and procedures of advanced contact lens materials and resources including their physiological implications.
Pediatric Optometry
Special aspects of the management of vision problems of infants and young children are discussed.
Visual Aspects of Leaming Difficulties

The aspects of vision problems related to learning difficulty including tests and measurements taken by optometrists. The role of the optometrist in conjunction with the parents, teachers, and psychologists in assisting children to achieve is discussed.
Prereq: Optom 242, 252, 402, 412

courses.label: OPTOM 504
courses.title: Ocutar Pharmacology
paras: Neurohumoral theory, response to drugs, sterile techniques, disinfectants. Drugs used in contact lens practice, drugs used topically on the eye, drugs on the eye and vision.
Prereq: Optom 404, 405, 415

courses.label: OPTOM 508
courses.title: Optometry Clinic
paras: The clinical programme teaches the student how to provide optometrical services inciuding pathology detection, strabismus evaluation and the application of spectacle therapy, contact lenses and vision training. The patients cared for extend from the pediatric to the geriatric, and include those with perceptual problems, or with low vision.
No credit given until successful completion of Optom 518.
Prereq: Permission of Clinic Director
Course Descriptions 415 Optometry

courses.label: OPTOM 509
courses.title: Community Health Optometry
paras: Governmental and social aspects of health and vision care delivery are discussed in relation to the epidemiology of vision problems.

courses.label: OPTOM 510
courses.title: Optometrical Jurisprudence
paras: Lectures relating to the legal aspects of practising optometry in Canada. The rights and responsibilities of the optometrist in practice are examined and discussed.

courses.label: OPTOM 511
courses.title: Optometry Research Project
paras: A continuation of 501. This course serves as an alternative to Optom 513.
Prereq: Optom 501

courses.label: OPTOM 512
courses.title: Advanced Contact Lens Practice
paras: A continuation of Optom 502 with an emphasis on research.
Visual Gerontology
Aspects of the aging process on the visual system and the optometrical management of the visual problems of older persons.
Recent Advances in Optometrical Technology and instrumentation
The use and interpretation of new resources for collecting, recording, analyzing and using optometrical data.

courses.label: OPTOM 513
courses.title: Optometric Communication
paras: Verbal communication and counselling during the optometrica! examination, alternatives to technical terminology, report and letter writing, preparing and delivering papers and taiks to professional societies and public information. ‘

courses.label: OPTOM 514
courses.title: Genetics for Optometrists
paras: A brief review of Mendelian genetics, and the molecular basis of modern genetics. Inherited conditions of particular interest, e.g., colour vision, albinism, aniridia, refractive error, retinoblastoma, etc. Genetic counselling, and the detection of carriers.
Prereq: Optom 405, 415

courses.label: OPTOM 518
courses.title: Optometry Clinic
paras: A continuation of 508 Prereq: Optom 508
24 Clinic 0.5

courses.label: OPTOM 519
paras: Aspects of prevention of accidents and injury to the visual system.
The production of efficient and comfortable vision at work and recreation.

courses.label: OPTOM 538
courses.title: Vision Care Projects
paras: All students are required to participate in vision care projects between the fourth and fifth professional years. These will involve a minimum of 400 hours and will be arranged by the faculty.
Prereq: Successful completion of Optometry 408 and 428 and permission of the Chief of Clinics.

Core Courses

The Core Courses for each year of the programme are designed to bring together students from various disciplines who are interested in the problems of conflict and peace, with the objective of acquainting them with other disciplinary approaches to those problems. Core courses are taught in Conrad Grebel College by members of the PACS Faculty Group, other qualified and interested members of participating departments, or by eminent scholars in the field who will be invited to the University from time to time.

courses.label: PACS 201
courses.title: Peace and Conflict Studies 1
paras: An examination of influential theories of the nature and roots of human conflict on both the interpersonal and inter-group level. Contributions of the behavioral and social sciences, as well as the humanities, will be expiored.
Brunk

courses.label: PACS 202
courses.title: Peace and Conflict Studies 2
paras: A continuation of PACS 201, with special emphasis on the means of conflict resolution or management. Included are critical assessments of negotiation, arbitration, confrontation, litigation, violence and nonviolent resistance, and other models of conflict resolution.
Brunk

courses.label: PACS 301
courses.title: Peace and Conflict Studies 3
paras: A seminar course investigating special issues related to peace and conflict. The content of this arid PACS 302 will vary from year to year as specialists in various aspects of these issues are invited to teach the courses.
Staff

courses.label: PACS 302
courses.title: Peace and Conflict Studies 4
paras: (Same as 301, above)
Staff

courses.label: PACS 498
courses.title: Senior Honours Seminar 1
paras: Each Honours student will work on a research paper and will meet regularly with other students working on similar projects to discuss and evaluate his own work.
Staff

courses.label: PACS 499
courses.title: Senlor Honours Seminar 2
paras: Continuation of PACS 498. Staff

paras: Psychology

courses.label: PHIL 100
courses.title: Introduction to Philosophy
paras: A broad selection of the main problems in philosophy will be considered. For example: How can we know whether anything is right or wrong? Can we know whether there is a God? Is mind in any sense distinct from matter? Original texts of both classical and contemporary thinkers are employed.

courses.label: PHIL 111
courses.title: Philosophy of Life
paras: “Who am I?” “What can | hope for after death?”
. “How can | tell what to do?” “What can | know?” are
questions that have ted people to philosophize. Approaches, such as those of the mystic, the scientist, the existentialist, the pleasure seeker, and the practical man, will be discussed.

courses.label: PHIL 120
courses.title: Science, Technology, and Society
paras: Alternative philosophical perspectives on problems raised by scientific and technological developments including moral issues (e.g. privacy and datagathering, ‘clean’ vs. ‘dirty’ energy.) Also an examination of the nature and scope of scientific and technical knowledge as it bears on the responsibilities of scientists and engineers.

courses.label: PHIL 125
courses.title: Introduction to Social and Political Philosophy
paras: An introduction to basic concepts and principles in classic and contemporary social and political philosophy. Differing views on basic questions are examined, with applications to such issues as capital punishment, welfare provisions, taxation, natural resource ownership, and terrorism.

courses.label: PHIL 135
courses.title: Introduction to the Philosophy of Religion
paras: Beginning with a consideration of such contemporary religious and anti-religious options as secularism, mysticism, occuitism, and charismatic renewal, this course moves to a critical discussion of such topics as religious experience, faith, God, and miracles.

courses.label: PHIL 140
courses.title: Introduction to Formal Logic
paras: Elementary sentence and predicate logic. Translation from English into the formalism,-decision methods and deductions. Application of Graphic Methods to Logic. This course is a preparation for courses in the foundations of mathematics, scientific methods, and more advanced logic courses.

courses.label: PHIL 145
courses.title: Critical Thinking
paras: An analysis of basic types of reasoning, structure of arguments, critical assessment of information, common fallacies, problems of clarity and meaning.

courses.label: PHIL 150
courses.title: Introduction: Knowledge and Reality
paras: Discussion of the nature of reality. Rival theories concerning mind, matter, freedom, the existence of God, and the place of experience and reason in human knowledge are considered.

courses.label: PHIL 200
courses.title: Great Works of Western Philosophy
paras: An examination of some of the greatest writings in Western Philosophy. Students will be encouraged tocome to a critical appreciation of such masterworksas Plato’s Republic, Descartes’ Discourse on Method, Hobbes’ Leviathan, Hume’s Enquiry, Kant’s Prolegomena, Nietzsche’s Zarathustra, and an outstanding work in contemporary philosophy.

courses.label: PHIL 200A
courses.title: Great Works of Western Philosophy: Part 1
paras: Outstanding works from the ancient and mediaeval periods.
Course Descriptions Phitosophy

courses.label: PHIL 200B
courses.title: Great Works of Western Philosophy: Part 11
paras: Outstanding works from the early modern and contemporary periods.
Note Either Phil 200A or Phil 200B may be taken separately.

courses.label: PHIL 201
courses.title: Love
paras: A philosophical analysis of different forms and functions of love. Among the topics to be considered: love and sexuality, religious love, love and knowledge. Ciassical and contemporary sources will be treated.

courses.label: PHIL 202
courses.title: Philosophy of Women
paras: A study of some of the issues raised by the Women’s Liberation movement. Philosophical writings of the past and present will be used on such subjects as: the two sexes, physiological femininity, personal and social relations between the sexes, the position of women in public life, marriage and its alternatives, the importance of childbearing.

courses.label: PHIL 203
courses.title: Philosophical Perspectives on Death
paras: This course critically examines how philosophers from the Pre-Socratics to Wittgenstein have analysed the concept of death. The course is also concerned with topics like the concept of a person, personal identity, and survival after death.

courses.label: PHIL 210
courses.title: Philosophy in Literature
paras: Each term philosophical themes (such as alienation, freedom, and responsibility) will be explored through appropriate literary works (e.g. works by Camus, Dostoevsky, Kafka, and Sartre).

courses.label: PHIL 215
courses.title: Professional and Business Ethics
paras: Study of ethical and moral issues that typically arise in professional and business activity. What ; responsibilities to society at large do people in such business and professional activities as teaching, engineering, planning, architecture, and accounting have? How far should professional autonomy extend?

courses.label: PHIL 216
courses.title: Rational Behaviour and Decision-Making
paras: An elementary introduction to the subject of ‘rational’ behaviour and decision-making for individuals and groups. Emphasis is on the definition and : measurement of utility functions and various criteria employed in models of decision-making. This course is intended to help those whose work will involve them in making decisions in either the public or private sectors.

courses.label: PHIL 220
courses.title: Moral Issues
paras: The aim of this course is to improve the student’s understanding of ethical ideas and principles by careful discussion of selected concrete moral issues, such as abortion, euthanasia, capital punishment, and violence. Choice of issues is partly determined by student interest. —

courses.label: PHIL 221
courses.title: Ethics 1
paras: This course is intended to be both a history of and an introduction to moral philosophy. Views on the foundations of ethics of the great philosophers from classical antiquity to about 1900 are systematically examined. Writers studied include: Plato, Aristotle, Aquinas, Kant, Mill and Nietzsche.

courses.label: PHIL 222
courses.title: Contemporary Ethical Theory
paras: Continues the history and discussion of ethics begun in Phil 221 with writings from 1900 to the present. Theories such as intuitionism, emotivism, utilitarianism, and relativism are examined via the writings of such people as Moore, Hare and Warnock. Prereq: 221 recommended

courses.label: PHIL 224
courses.title: Mankind and Nature
paras: An examination of some of the issues raised by recent discussions on ecology. Various theories of nature, the human being, and relations between the two will be explored. Possible foundations for duties of mankind toward nature will be examined.

courses.label: PHIL 225
courses.title: Social and Politica! Philosophy: Canadian Problems
paras: Basic ideological perspectives - conservative, socialist, and liberal - on Canadian problems - such as native rights, nationalism, separatism, and regionalism - are philosophically presented and assessed.
Prereq: Philosophy 125 or consent of the instructor.
Course Descriptions 421 Philosophy

courses.label: PHIL 226
courses.title: Ethics and the Life Sciences
paras: An investigation of some critical ethical issues in human research and therapy. Includes discussions of the right to live and right to die, behavior control (e.g. psychosurgery, behavior modification and psychotherapy), human experimentation (including “informed consent” and fetal research) and genetic engineering.
Prereq: One of Phil 125, 221, 222, or consent of instructor

courses.label: PHIL 236
courses.title: Philosophy of Religion: The Occult
paras: A criticat philosophical discussion of reports of several kinds of extraordinary experiences, such as magic, extra-sensory perception, mysticism, and divination will lead us to discussions of such concepts as insanity, irrationality, the supernatural, . and the miraculous.

courses.label: PHIL 240
courses.title: Logic
paras: A systematic development of the propositional calculus and of the first-order functional caiculus. Some attention will be devoted to extensions and interpretations of such formal systems.
Prereq: None for second-year students and above; consent of instructor for others.

courses.label: PHIL 241
courses.title: Intermediate Logic
paras: Axiom systems of iogic are developed and compared with natural deduction procedures. Then certainproperties of these logical systems, such as consistency, completeness, and compactness, will be investigated.
Prereq: Phil 140 or consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 242
courses.title: Extensions and Applications of Elementary Logic
paras: The classical logic introduced in Phil 140 will be extended to form systems of modal logic, including logics of obligation, belief and knowledge, necessity, and temporal order. Essentialism, future contingencies, proofs for the existence of God will be discussed.
Prereq: Phil 140 or consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 243
courses.title: Risk, Decision, Games, Amalgamation
paras: Fundamentals of probability and game theory. Problems of decision making under conditions of certainty, risk and uncertainty. The definition and measurement of utility functions. Translation of decisions and preferences of members of a group into collective preference. Some applications to the Social Sciences.
Prereq: Phil 140, 145 or consent of instructor

courses.label: PHIL 258
courses.title: Introduction to the Philosophy of Science
paras: A discussion.of the fundamental concepts on which science is based. Consideration is given to such topics as scientific explanation, the structure of
- scientific theories, the nature of law-likeness, the
grounds for scientific confirmation, and the debate between rationalism and empiricism in science.

courses.label: PHIL 265
courses.title: The Existentialist Experience
paras: An introduction to the existentialist view of man using both literary and philosophical texts from such authors as Kierkegaard, Unamuno, Nietzsche, Ortega y Gasset, Camus, Sartre, Heidegger and others. Offered in August at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PHIL 270
courses.title: Special Topics in Philosophy
paras: Not offered 1981-82

courses.label: PHIL 280
courses.title: History of Ancient Philosophy 1
paras: From the beginnings to Plato.
Prereq: Second year standing or above, or consent of instructor

courses.label: PHIL 281
courses.title: History of Ancient Philosophy 2
paras: From Aristotle to the close of classical antiquity. Prereq: Phil 280

courses.label: PHIL 282
courses.title: History of Modern Philosophy 1
paras: Earlier period beginning with Descartes.
Prereq: Second year standing or above, or consent of instructor

courses.label: PHIL 283
courses.title: History of Modern Philosophy 2
paras: Later period including Hume and Kant.
Prereq: Second year standing or above, or consent of instructor. Phil 282 recommended.
Course Descriptions Philosophy

courses.label: PHIL 284
courses.title: 19th Century Philosophy
paras: The 19th century. Philosophers covered may include Hegel, Mill, Schopenhauer, James, and Kierkegaard.

courses.label: PHIL 285
courses.title: 20th Century Philosophy
paras: A course intended to introduce the student to the dominent themes of 20th century philosophy, centering on the major figures of this century, such as Bertrand Russell, Ludwig Wittgenstein, G. E. Moore, Edmund Husserl, and Jean-Paul Sartre.

courses.label: PHIL 300
courses.title: The Philosophy of Games
paras: An introduction to philosophical issues relating to sports and other games. Among the issues examined will be the nature of games, games and sports, and the relevance of games and sports to other philosophical interests: e.g., ethics and aesthetics.

courses.label: PHIL 311
courses.title: Philosophy of Education 1
paras: A philosophical analysis of classical and contemporary theories of education, with a view to formulating a clear workable concept of education, its aims and methods.
Prereq: At least second year standing or consent of instructor

courses.label: PHIL 312
courses.title: Philosophy of Education 2
paras: An introduction to current work in the field, particularly that of Peters, Hirst, and Dearden. Special attention will be paid to the question of the desirability of a core curriculum and its proposed content.
Prereq: Phil 311 or consent of instructor

courses.label: PHIL 321
courses.title: Studies in Ethics
paras: Various half courses dealing with special topics; one or more of these will be offered each year as announced by the Department.
Prereq: Phil 221/222. See Note 1

courses.label: PHIL 325
courses.title: Political Philosophy 1
paras: Philosophical analysis of central concepts in political theory and its relation to moral and metaphysical problems of various periods.
Prereq: Phil 125 or consent of the instructor

courses.label: PHIL 326
courses.title: Political Philosophy 2
paras: A detailed discussion of contemporary theories. Prereq: Phil 125 or consent of the instructor

courses.label: PHIL 327A
courses.title: Philosophy of Law - Part 1
paras: An investigation of alternative views of law and legal reasoning forms the core of this course. Law’s relations to morality, social practice, and politics are considered. Authors to be studied include Aquinas, Kant, Austin, and Hart.
Prereq: Phil 221 or another approved values course, or consent of the instructor.
Note This is a required course for the Legal Studies Option.

courses.label: PHIL 327B
courses.title: Philosophy of Law - Part 2
paras: An examination of areas within the law in which philosophical problems and methods are featured prominently. Topics such as liberty, responsibility and liability, punishment, rights and possession are considered..
Prereq: Phil 327A or consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 328
courses.title: The Philosophy of Karl Marx
paras: Not offered 1981-82

courses.label: PHIL 329
courses.title: War, Peace and Justice
paras: An intensive study of the moral issues involved in war and armed revolution. Critical evaluation of “just war” theories, and international rules of warfare is pursued as well as the moral arguments for and against pacifism and conscientious objection. Prereq: Phil 125, or 221/222, or consent of instructor

courses.label: PHIL 331
courses.title: Aesthetics
paras: Philosophical consideration of works of art and the problems of beauty using selected readings to enable the student to recognize and formulate his own views in a philosophic manner.
Prereq: One full or two half Philosophy courses, or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 335
courses.title: Philosophy of Religion
paras: A critical examination of the methods and substantive arguments found in selected major works of religious philosophy. The writings chosen for consideration will be announced in advance each year.
Prereq: One full or two half Philosophy courses, or consent of instructor.
See Note 1.
Course Descriptions , 423 Philosophy

courses.label: PHIL 340
courses.title: Logical Theory
paras: A rigorous and general development of the propositional and predicate calculus within which alternative calculi are examined. Study of such concepts as completeness, consistency, extensionality, and modality from both formal and philosophical points of view. Intended primarily for those interested in philosophical issues connected with logic.
Prereq: Phil 140, or (preferably) Phil 240, 241 or 242, or consent of instructor

courses.label: PHIL 350
courses.title: Epistemology
paras: An analysis of human knowledge, its conditions and types. The first part concentrates on criteria of meaningfulness, the possibility of 2 priori knowledge, and the concept of knowledge. The second part deals with our knowledge of the physical world and other minds.
Prereq: One full or two half courses in Philosophy.

courses.label: PHIL 350A
courses.title: Epistemology 1
paras: The first part of Phil 350.

courses.label: PHIL 350B
courses.title: Epistemology 2
paras: The second part of Phil 350.
Note . Either 350A or 350B may be taken separately.

courses.label: PHIL 359
courses.title: Philosophy of the Formal Sciences
paras: A study of philosophical problems concerning mathematics. Topics discussed include formalism, intuitionism, logicism, the mathematical paradoxes, and other topics in foundations and metamathematics.
Prereq: At least second year standing or consent of instructor

courses.label: PHIL 362
courses.title: Philosophy of the Social Sciences
paras: Problems about the fundamental methods and aims of the social sciences generally, and problems specific to Psychology, Sociology, Political Science, etc., and their relations to one another will be considered.
(Cross-listed as Soc 371)

courses.label: PHIL 363
courses.title: Philosophy of Language and Linguistic Analysis
paras: The first part examines issues in the philosophy of language, such as synonymy, propositions, meaning, semantics, reference. The second part will consider ordinary language analysis as a method for solving philosophical problems as compared with structural linguistics.
Prereq: At least second year standing or consent of instructor

courses.label: PHIL 363A
courses.title: Philosophy of Language
paras: The first part of Phil 363.

courses.label: PHIL 363B
courses.title: Linguistic Analysis
paras: The second part of Phii 363.
Note Either Phil 363A or Phil 363B may be taken separately.

courses.label: PHIL 365
courses.title: Oriental Philosophy
paras: Studies of a selected area of non-western Philosophy (e.g. Indian or Chinese). Parallels will be drawn between modes of Eastern thinking and European conceptions with emphasis on essential differences as well as similarities.
Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: PHIL 370
courses.title: Special Subjects
paras: One or more half courses will be offered at different times as announced by the Department.
Prereq: Consent of instructor. See Note 1

courses.label: PHIL 380
courses.title: Studies in the History of Philosophy
paras: Various half courses dealing with a particular philosopher, a selected work or period; one or more of these will be offered each year as announced by the Department.
Prereq: Appropriate course(s) from Phit 280-285 or Phil 390/391, or consent of instructor.
See Note 1

courses.label: PHIL 390
courses.title: Medieval Philosophy 1
paras: The early period of the 13th century. Among those considered will be: Augustine, Boethius, Anselm, and Abailard.
Prereq: one full or two half courses in Philosophy
Course Descriptions Philosophy —

courses.label: PHIL 391
courses.title: Medieval Philosophy 2
paras: The later period from the 13th century. Among those considered will be: Bonaventure, Aquinas, Scotus, and Ockham.
Prereq: Phil 390

courses.label: PHIL 398A
courses.title: Directed Reading in Special Areas
paras: Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: PHIL 309
courses.title: Tutorial for Honours Students
paras: Students wishing to enrol in 399 should consult the Department.

courses.label: PHIL 425
courses.title: Philosophy of the City
paras: Analysis and evaluation of the philosophical points of view that underlie current criticism of urban life and prevalent schemes for its reconstruction.
Prereq: One half Philosophy course

courses.label: PHIL 435
courses.title: Students in Philosophy of Religion
paras: A study of a particular philosopher or problem. The topic will be announced in advance each year. Prereq: Consent of instructor. See Note 1

courses.label: PHIL 440
courses.title: Studies in Logic
paras: Various half courses dealing with specific topics; one or more of these will be offered each year as announced by the Department.
Prereq: Phil 240, 241, 242 or 340 or PMath 430a.
See Note 1

courses.label: PHIL 446
courses.title: Philesophy of History
paras: Consideration of various possible views about ultimate nature of history and historical knowledge. Offered in sequence with Hist 466.
Prereq: One full course equivalent in Philosophy, or consent of instructor

courses.label: PHIL 455
courses.title: Metaphysics
paras: Studies of reality, metaphysical problems and issues. The first part ontology (nature of being) considers objects, their properties, and causation. The second part cosmology (principles of the universe) examines space, time, and motion.

courses.label: PHIL 455A
courses.title: Ontology
paras: The first part of Phil 455.

courses.label: PHIL 455B
courses.title: Cosmology
paras: The second part of Phil 455.
Note Either Phil 455A or Phil 455B may be taken separately.

courses.label: PHIL 465
courses.title: Existential Philosophy
paras: Not offered 1981-82.

courses.label: PHIL 470
courses.title: Phenomenology
paras: Not offered 1981-82..

courses.label: PHIL 471
courses.title: Problems
paras: One or more half courses will be offered at different times, as announced by the Department.
Prereq: Consent of instructor. See Note 17

courses.label: PHIL 480
courses.title: Advanced Studies in the History of Philosophy
paras: Various half courses dealing with a particular philosopher, a selected work or period; one or more of these will be offered each year as announced by. the Department.
Prereq: Consent of instructor. See Note 7

courses.label: PHIL 498
courses.title: Directed Reading in Speciai Areas
paras: Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: PHIL 499
courses.title: Tutorial and Honours Essay
paras: Students wishing to enrol in 499 should consult the Department.
The following courses are administered by St. Jerome’s College

courses.label: PHIL 100J
courses.title: Introduction to Philosophy
paras: A broad selection of the main problems in philosophy will be considered. For example: how can we know whether anything is right or wrong? How can we know about things we cannot directly observe? Can we know whether there is a God? !s mind in any sense distinct from matter?

courses.label: PHIL 120J
courses.title: Philosophy of Life and Death
paras: A study of what some of the great philosophers have said about the meaning of life and death and the transition from life to death. Students are urged to raise questions and help direct discussion.
Offered in the evening.
Course Descriptions 425 Philosophy

courses.label: PHIL 130J
courses.title: Philosophy of Discontent
paras: A study of what some of the great philosophers have said about the causes of discontent. Social disobedience and the extent to which ethical principles can be altered to accommodate changing conditions are possible topics for discussion. — Offered in the evening.

courses.label: PHIL 200J
courses.title: Intentional Logic
paras: An introduction to the understanding of how words are used, the formation of propositions, the construction of arguments and the examination of fallacies to help the student to argue with order, with facility and without error.

courses.label: PHIL 205J
courses.title: Philosophy of Nature
paras: An examination of ancient and modern accounts of the. natura! world. Problems include whether matter alone can account for change, whether there is more than one cause, whether nature operates by purpose or chance.

courses.label: PHIL 210J
courses.title: Philosophy of Man
paras: What is man? What is man’s place among other creatures? Is man an accident of evolution? What are the major views on man as a species? How are love and sex aspects of man’s life?

courses.label: PHIL 218J
courses.title: Ethical Theory
paras: A normative approach, employing several of the classic Western traditions of rational thought, to general ethics. The various schools of ethical thought will be discussed.
Also offered in the evening.

courses.label: PHIL 219J
courses.title: Practical Ethics
paras: This course will discuss the applications of general ethics to more specific areas of human endeavour: Among the topics discussed will be abortion, contraception, sex, obscenity, violence, drugs, egoism, dishonesty, and various forms of human exploitation.
Also offered in the evening winter term.

courses.label: PHIL 230J
courses.title: God and Philosophy
paras: An investigation of several aspects concerning the meaning and existence of God. Is God-talk possible? Can faith and reason be reconciled? Is religious experience a meaningful argument? A wide range of different views will be considered.
Offered in the evening.

courses.label: PHIL 237J
courses.title: Ethics and Society ~
paras: Examines the nature and purpose of community living as well as such traditionally controversial issues as private and public morality, the individual good and the common good, personal freedom and group responsibility.
Offered in the evening.

courses.label: PHIL 260J
courses.title: Issues in Higher Education
paras: Why go to university? What are the present realities in Canada? What is the role of the liberal arts? The primary interest will be upon what can be done in practice rather than upon ideal schemes.
Offered in the evening.

courses.label: PHIL 300J
courses.title: The Western Philosophical Tradition (to 1600)
paras: An intensive overview of the major recurring themes in Western intellectual history from both an historical and a philosophical viewpoint.
Prereq: Second year standing.

courses.label: PHIL 301J
courses.title: The Western Philosophical Tradition (1600-Present)
paras: A continuation of 300J. Descartes to Existentialism. Prereq: Second year standing.

courses.label: PHIL 318J
courses.title: Philosophy of the Family
paras: Not offered 1981-82.

courses.label: PHIL 333J
courses.title: Contemporary Philosophical Problems in
paras: Art Not offered in 1981-82.

courses.label: PHIL 395J
courses.title: The Thomistic Tradition in Philosophy
paras: Not offered 1981-82

courses.title: Special Topics/Directed Readings
paras: A series of readings and/or seminars on one or two topics or thinkers, with periodic reports and discussion.
Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.title: Tutorial

courses.label: PHIL 450J
courses.title: Being and Existence
paras: An advanced course for the serious student, delving into the notions of reality, being, essence, existence, analogy, etc. The techniques of linguistic analysis will be employed. Also, the very possibility of any kind of metaphysics will be discussed.
Prereq: Third year standing or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 496J
courses.title: Special Topics/Directed Readings
paras: A series of readings and/or seminars on one or two topics or thinkers, with periodic reports and discussions.
Prereq: Consent of instructor.

Course Descriptions
